back: Humans choose individuals with desired traits to breed, increasing the frequency of the alleles for those traits.
Reduced vigour and fertility from inbreeding, as harmful recessive alleles become homozygous.
Greater growth or yield of hybrids than of either parent, from heterozygosity at many loci.

front: Why F1 hybrid maize is uniform
back: Both inbred parents are homozygous, so all F1 plants have the same genotype.

front: Why hybrid seed is bought each year
back: Saved F1 seed gives a variable F2 with lower yield because alleles segregate.
Judging a male's genetic merit from the performance of his offspring, e.g. daughters' milk yields.

front: Breeding disease resistance into wheat or rice
back: Cross with a resistant variety, then backcross repeatedly to the high-yielding parent, selecting resistant offspring.
Loss of genetic diversity, making crops and breeds vulnerable to new diseases or conditions.
